title: F1 four-mode model research v2
description: Chronological 2026 evidence for the Qualifying, race-final-position, Best-Lap, and Live F1 model review.

blocks.body:
# F1 four-mode model research v2

A model being implemented is not the same as it being selected, promoted, or deployed. These results use race weekends as the independent validation unit and preserve the retained baseline whenever a challenger does not clear its evidence gate. Forecasts are target-isolated within each replay, but R7-R9 are postdevelopment diagnostics rather than pristine prospective evidence.

## Evidence decisions

Qualifying's research winner is shared latent v4 plus MEAL, but the public output is the rehearsal-rank baseline because the challenger ties it on R7-R9. The main Race survival challenger loses on rank, MAE, Brier, and log loss; an ablation bound to nine parsed official FIA grid PDFs covers R1-R9 but adds no edge. Each PDF header is converted from a pinned venue timezone to UTC and the claimed publication lag must be 0-300 seconds; all nine pass, with a maximum observed lag of 60 seconds. The Best-Lap challenger is 1.76% worse and its interval is 31.45% wider. The true bounded TCN was trained, but its post-development profiles are outer-target-informed and parameter-sensitive, so its nested selector retains zero correction. Live uses state v6, transition/replay/dataset v8, and legal-mask v3. Pit-now needs one remaining lap and pit-next-lap needs two; known inventory must contain a reachable mandatory compound, and terminal states have no constraint action. Constraint legality remains authoritative while a separately tagged, explicitly penalized nonlegal operational fallback is excluded from learning and learned-policy selection. The replay contains 9,506 partial-label BC rows but zero offline-Q or propensity-OPE rows, and rolling BC exactly ties the trivial classifier.

## Methodology

All comparisons are same-season and chronological. Selection, calibration, and replay partitions are disjoint within each current run. They are not independent of earlier development exposure: implementation defects were corrected after R7-R9 had been inspected. The public output remains the baseline when a candidate loses, and formal promotion requires future prospective rounds.

charts.title: R7-R9 postdevelopment replay MAE by mode, round, and model

query.description: Read the notebook-exported long-form R7-R9 postdevelopment replay MAE rows.
query.sql: SELECT mode, round, mode || ' R' || CAST(round AS VARCHAR) AS round_label, unit, CASE WHEN series = 'baseline' THEN 'Retained baseline' ELSE 'Challenger' END AS series, mae FROM read_csv_auto('docs/research/evidence/f1_audit_comparison_long_2026.csv') ORDER BY mode, round, series
metric_definitions: mae is event-level mean absolute error on the R7-R9 postdevelopment replay; units are positions for Qualifying and the main Race survival model and seconds for Best lap

query.description: Read the bounded mode-decision snapshot embedded with the report.
query.sql: SELECT mode_order, mode, implemented, selected, promoted, runtime FROM mode_decisions ORDER BY mode_order
